pageTitle: What's not in Gravita — and why
pageIntro: We'd rather do fewer movements properly than list hundreds we can't actually coach. Here's what we left out and the honest reason.

sections.title: Gym machines
sections.userReason: Machines already fix the path your body travels, so there is very little form left for a camera to judge — and the frame usually hides your torso behind the machine. We would be guessing, so we don't include them.

sections.title: Flips, aerials and tumbling
sections.userReason: These carry a real risk of a catastrophic fall. An app that cannot spot you should not be the thing that tells you you're ready.

sections.title: One-rep max and strength testing
sections.userReason: A camera cannot measure force. We can count your reps and track them over time, and you can compare those numbers to published strength standards — but we will never tell you we measured your strength.

sections.title: Injury diagnosis and rehab prescriptions
sections.userReason: Gravita is a movement-practice tool, not a medical service. If something hurts, we tell you to stop — we don't tell you why.

sections.title: Training with a partner in frame
sections.userReason: We analyse one person per session. A second body in the frame makes the analysis unreliable, so we ask you to clear the frame instead of quietly guessing which skeleton is yours.
searchTerms: training with a partner in frame

sections.title: Tracking the equipment itself
sections.userReason: We coach your body, not your gear. For these movements we watch your mechanics — the landing, the hinge, the line — but we don't detect the box, the rope or the bar.

sections.title: Form scoring on bench press (and similar lying pressing)
sections.userReason: You lie down and press away from the camera, so the phone is looking straight down the path of the movement. Depth and bar path can't be judged honestly from that angle. We count your reps, time your tempo and check your setup — and we say so on the movement page.
